Attackers can send base64-encoded 'root' to POST /admin/login when NP_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD is unset to obtain admin tokens and fully control the site.

Sandboxie-Plus before 1.18.6 contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability in SbieSvc that allows standard users to launch UpdUtil.exe as SYSTEM via MSGID_PROCESS_RUN_UPDATER requests. Attackers can inject code into a signed SandMan.exe process to bypass the signature check and write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary paths, achieving SYSTEM code execution.

The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server reports every request as authenticated when an application requests authentication programmatically. A remote unauthenticated attacker can access functionality protected this way. Only applications served by the embedded HTTP server that rely on programmatic authentication are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

The Wikidata Lookup expansion module (wiki.py) in MISP misp-modules contained a SPARQL injection vulnerability. The handler function constructed a SPARQL query by directly concatenating the user-supplied text value into the query string without any escaping or parameterization: 'SELECT ?item WHERE { ?item rdfs:label"' + request.get("text") + '" @en }'. An authenticated MISP user with access to the module could supply a crafted text attribute value containing SPARQL syntax (quotes, closing braces, UNION, SERVICE, LIMIT, etc.) to alter the structure of the query sent to the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint. This could allow an attacker to modify the query logic, extract unintended data, or cause the query to fail in ways that expose internal error details. Additionally, the old error handling path formatted raw exception objects into the response string ('wikidata API not accessible {}'.format(e)), potentially leaking internal information such as proxy credentials, query contents, or response bodies. The module also used a spoofed browser user-agent string and the deprecated Wikidata endpoint. The vulnerability required authenticated access to the MISP instance and the ability to invoke the wiki expansion module with a text attribute. The impact is limited to manipulation of the enrichment query and potential disclosure of internal error details; it does not directly compromise the MISP server or its stored data.

Building a malicious package that uses cgo could cause arbitrary code execution at link time by passing linker script files to the host linker via "#cgo LDFLAGS". Split "-Wl," flags that consume a following argument (such as "-Wl,-rpath", "-Wl,--just-symbols", and "-Wl,-undefined") previously accepted a bare second argument without a "-Wl," prefix, which the compiler driver passes directly to the linker as a positional input file. Additionally, when using GNU ld.bfd, flags such as "-framework", "-Wl,-framework", "-Wl,-undefined", "-Wl,--just-symbols", "-Wl,-R", "-Wl,-subsystem", and (on non-Darwin platforms) "-Wl,-sectcreate" could cause ld.bfd to interpret their arguments as linker scripts if they named a regular file on disk. The go command now requires a "-Wl," prefix on the second token of split "-Wl," flags (except "-Wl,-R"), verifies that these flags do not reference linker script files, and disallows bare "-Wl,--warn-backrefs-exclude".

The MISP Modules website component exposes external tool management endpoints (add, delete, change status, and change configuration) that did not enforce the optional administrator authentication policy. When ADMIN_PASSWORD was configured in the application environment, the module configuration endpoints correctly required an authenticated administrator session, but the external tools management handlers processed requests from anonymous users without any authorization check. An unauthenticated attacker with network access to the website could add arbitrary external tools, delete existing tools, toggle their active status, and modify their configurations including API keys and ingestion URLs. This inconsistency allowed bypass of the intended access control for the external tools management functionality. The vulnerability is conditional on ADMIN_PASSWORD being set; installations without an admin password intentionally permit open management access by design. The affected component is the external_tools Flask blueprint within the MISP Modules website application.

The admin service of the standalone OpenEJB server accepts stop requests without any authentication. Any local user or process able to connect to the admin port can stop the server, leading to denial of service; the admin service is enabled by default in the standalone server and bound to the loopback interface. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

Building a malicious package containing ".syso" files or cgo linker inputs could inject arbitrary linker flags or execute arbitrary code at link time. Linker input files—including ".syso" files, direct object or library inputs in "#cgo LDFLAGS", and libraries in "-L" directories—were passed to the external linker without validating their format or checking for embedded linker options. Across platforms, this allowed executing GNU ld implicit linker scripts disguised as libraries or ".syso" files (or loaded via "-l:<filename>" or "-l" containing path separators), injecting unallowlisted linker flags via PE/COFF ".drectve" sections on Windows or Mach-O "LC_LINKER_OPTION" load commands on Darwin, or invoking LTO plugins via GCC or LLVM LTO intermediate representation sections in ELF, PE/COFF, or Mach-O objects. The go command now verifies that ".syso" files, direct linker inputs, and libraries in "-L" directories are valid binary objects or archives that do not contain unallowlisted ".drectve" directives, "LC_LINKER_OPTION" load commands, or LTO IR sections, and disallows "-l:<filename>" and ":", "=", or path separators in "-l" flags.

The MISP Modules website component contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the external tools management interface. The /external_tools/list endpoint returned stored API keys (the api_key field) in its JSON response via the ExternalTools model serializer. Additionally, the browser-based edit form pre-populated the API key input field with the stored credential value, exposing it in the DOM.

The /external_tools/list endpoint is accessible without authentication (the regression tests verify the response for both authenticated and unauthenticated clients), meaning any network-reachable client could retrieve the API keys for all configured external tools. These keys are used by the server to authenticate submissions to external analysis or enrichment services, so their disclosure allows an attacker to impersonate the MISP instance or directly access those external services.

The vulnerability also affected the edit workflow: the change_config endpoint previously required the API key to be present and non-empty on every save, forcing the key to round-trip through the client. The browser JavaScript stored the key in a reactive state object and updated the in-memory tool list with the credential value, further increasing the window of exposure in client-side memory and network traffic.

Affected component: the website sub-application of MISP Modules, specifically the external_tools module (serializer in models.py, list endpoint, and the external_tools_index.html template). The impact is limited to confidentiality of the stored API keys; no integrity or availability impact on the MISP Modules website itself is indicated by the patch.

When JAX-WS or JAX-RS endpoints are published by the embedded OpenEJB HTTP server rather than Tomcat, some configured authentication methods are silently ignored and the endpoint is published without authentication. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed operations without credentials. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server and rely on such an authentication method are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

The MISP Modules website component contains an open redirect vulnerability in its login endpoint. The /login route accepted a user-supplied next query parameter and passed it directly to Flask's redirect() function without validating the destination. An attacker could craft a URL such as https://victim-host/login?next=https://attacker.example/phish and deliver it to a user (e.g., via email or a lookalike page). After the user successfully authenticated, the application issued a 302 redirect to the attacker-controlled external URL. This enables phishing attacks where a user, believing they are still on the legitimate MISP Modules site, may enter additional credentials or sensitive information on the attacker's page. It can also be used to obscure the true destination of a link, bypassing user trust in the legitimate domain. The vulnerability requires the victim to interact with the crafted URL and complete a login, but no prior authentication or special configuration is needed on the attacker's side. The affected component is the website sub-project of misp-modules, specifically the account blueprint in website/app/account/account.py. No version boundaries are specified in the patch metadata.

With the default configuration and no users defined in the default user database, TomEE silently adds an administrative user with a well-known password at startup. A remote attacker can use these credentials to authenticate to web applications that use the default realm and grant access to any authenticated user or to the TomEE administrative role. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the authentication decorators for feed-key requests (auth_feedkey_func in website/decorators.py) and API-key requests (auth_func in website/web/api/v1/common.py) called Flask-Login's login_user() function. This caused the HTTP response to a request authenticated solely by a feed key (supplied as the X-FEED-KEY URL parameter) or an API key (supplied as the X-API-KEY header) to set a session cookie that grants full authenticated access to every page in the application, without requiring a password or two-factor authentication.

The practical impact is that any party possessing a leaked feed URL (a common occurrence, as feed URLs are shared with RSS readers) or an API key could obtain a valid web session for the associated account. This session provides access to the user's account page, which exposes the API key and other profile data, and for accounts with the administrator role, access to the /admin interface, enabling full administrative control of the application.

The vulnerability affects all users whose feed key or API key is exposed. No prior authentication, user interaction, or special network conditions are required; a single HTTP request with the token is sufficient to establish the session. The session persists until it expires, and because it is not bound to the original credential (a related CWE-613 issue noted by the developers), revoking the feed key or API key does not invalidate the already-created session.

The fix replaces the login_user() call with assignment to g._login_user, which Flask-Login's current_user property reads for the current request only, without writing any session cookie. The affected views remain unchanged and continue to see the authenticated user for the single request.

In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the Flask-Login session identifier was set to the bare numeric user ID (User.get_id() returned self.id). Because the session ID contained no component derived from the user's credential, it remained valid indefinitely regardless of any subsequent password change, account recovery, or administrator-initiated password reset. An attacker who had obtained a valid session for a user account (for example through cross-site scripting, session hijacking, or a previously exposed feed or API key) could continue to access that user's account after the user changed their password, because the session cookie still carried the same static user ID and the user_loader accepted it without any credential-bound validation.

The affected component is the session management layer of the vulnerability-lookup Flask application, specifically the User.get_id() method in website/models/user.py and the load_user callback in website/web/views/session_mgmt.py. The vulnerability required that an attacker already possessed a valid session for the target user; no additional authentication or special deployment configuration was needed beyond a standard deployment of the application.

The security impact is that a user cannot effectively revoke an attacker's access by changing their password, performing an account recovery, or having an administrator reset the credential. The attacker retains full authenticated access to the user's profile, subscriptions, and any role-gated functionality for the lifetime of the session cookie. Additionally, sessions that were opened via a feed key or API key before a prior fix (commit 3605d5b6) also persisted indefinitely.

Kunai, a security monitoring tool, contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in its mount namespace (mnt ns) caching logic. When resolving a security event that references a specific process PID and an expected mount namespace, the Switcher::new function read /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt to determine the target namespace and cached the result under the expected namespace key without verifying that the resolved namespace actually matched the expected one.

An attacker with local access could exploit this by either (1) arranging for the referenced PID to be reused by a process in a different namespace (e.g., the host namespace) before Kunai resolves it, or (2) calling unshare or setns on the target process after the event is generated but before the namespace is resolved. In either case, the wrong namespace (potentially the host's own namespace) would be cached under the container's namespace key.

The security impact is that subsequent container security events would be resolved against host filesystem paths rather than container paths. This undermines the integrity of the security monitoring data: container activity could be misattributed to the host, host activity could be misattributed to a container, and file-path-based detections or alerts would reference incorrect paths. An attacker could potentially use this to obscure malicious activity within a container by making it appear as benign host activity, or to generate misleading security alerts.

The vulnerability requires local access to the system and a specific timing window between event generation and namespace resolution. No remote attack vector or user interaction is required.

The optional request routing feature forwards requests to their configured destination without applying the security constraints of that destination or the protection of the web application's private directories. If a route copies client-controlled parts of the request path into its destination, a remote attacker can reach protected resources or read application configuration and class files. Only installations with such a routing configuration are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

Building a malicious package that uses cgo could bypass "#cgo LDFLAGS" validation and cause unexpected code execution at build time, or cause the go command to panic, via crafted quoting in "//go:cgo_ldflag" directives. When "cmd/cgo" generates "_cgo_gotypes.go", it quotes each "#cgo LDFLAGS" argument with strconv.Quote in a "//go:cgo_ldflag" directive, but "cmd/compile" and "cmd/go" parsed those directives by splitting on raw quote characters without handling backslash escapes or unquoting the string. This mismatch allowed disallowed linker flags or unvalidated linker search paths to be smuggled past the go command's flag checks and passed to the external linker. In addition, deduplicating LDFLAGS in the go command could panic with an out-of-bounds slice index when a prefix of the flag list matched near the end of the slice. "cmd/compile" and "cmd/go" now properly handle backslash-escaped quotes and unquote "//go:cgo_*" pragma strings with strconv.Unquote, and the slice bounds check in processCgoOutputs has been fixed.

The remote EJB client does not verify that the hostname of the server it connects to matches the server's TLS certificate. An attacker able to intercept network traffic between an EJB client and server can impersonate the server and read or modify the traffic, including credentials and invocation data. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
Invalid Memory Access via the MSI-X table in QVM could allow an attacker in the guest to execute arbitrary code in the QVM to cause memory corruption, information disclosure or a crash of the QVM.

Untrusted search path in the cross-user process launcher in Open Job Description (OpenJD) Sessions for Python before 0.11.0, as used in the AWS Deadline Cloud worker agent before 0.33.0, on Linux might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to submit jobs to a queue to execute arbitrary code as the worker agent OS user and obtain the AWS credentials held by the worker agent via a crafted job that modifies the PATH environment variable.



To remediate this issue, users of customer-managed fleets should upgrade the Deadline Cloud worker agent to version 0.33.0 or later, which includes OpenJD Sessions 0.11.0. Service-managed fleets were remediated service-side.

The embedded Derby network service ignores its configured bind address and listens on all network interfaces. When the service is enabled, a remote attacker with network access can connect to the database server and read or modify data. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

The LeRobot library is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution via unsafe dynamic class instantiation in the from_pretrained() method and related paths. When loading a policy's processor configuration from a repository,  the library uses the class field within the JSON configuration to dynamically resolve and instantiate Python classes using importlib.import_module() and getattr().

The Shipo plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions 1.6 through 1.8.0. This is due to the `authenticate_rest_user()` function parsing the `LOGGED_IN_COOKIE` value and authenticating the named user without verifying the cookie's cryptographic signature. The function's intended `/wp-json/shipo/` route restriction can also be bypassed by placing that substring in the query string of an unrelated REST endpoint. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know an existing username to impersonate that user, including an administrator, and perform authorized actions through the REST API, including creating another administrator account.

The EJBd remote protocol returns datasource connection details, including database credentials, to remote clients that look up a datasource. A remote client able to reach the EJBd endpoint can obtain the database credentials and connect to the database directly. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

When Hessian remoting endpoints are served by the embedded HTTP server, configured authentication and transport security requirements are silently ignored. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods without credentials or over an unencrypted connection. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server rather than Tomcat and rely on these settings are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.

When Hessian remoting is configured with BASIC authentication, the authentication check is not applied to Hessian endpoints of applications deployed under a non-root context path. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods without credentials. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.

A authorization bypass through user-controlled key vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer 7.2.0 through 7.2.12, FortiAnalyzer 7.0 all versions, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.12, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.0 all versions, FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.12, FortiManager 7.0 all versions, FortiManager Cloud 8.0.1, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.12, FortiManager Cloud 7.0 all versions may allow an authenticated administrator to access to other VDOMs via specially crafted HTTP requests.

Dell Display and Peripheral Manager (DDPM Windows), versions prior to 2.4.0.17, contain a Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Condition vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code execution.

Trimble SketchUp SKP File Parsing Use-After-Free Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Trimble SketchUp. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of SKP files. The issue results from the lack of validating the existence of an object prior to performing operations on the object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-30421.

User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of XE files. The issue results from the lack of validating the existence of an object prior to performing operations on the object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28757.

Philips Hue Bridge Pro Argument Injection Restricted File Write Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to modify files on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge Pro. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code within a container on the target system, in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the factory data service, which listens on TCP port 5001 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to modify files in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-33090.

Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in RsPressMiddleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private documentation by supplying any non-empty viewToken cookie. Attackers can send requests with a forged viewToken cookie, which is never validated as a JWT, to read all pages and assets of RequireAuth documentation sites.
Missing authentication in Ivanti Cloud Services Application version 5.0.8 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to add and delete arbitrary trusted EPM Core certificate entries.

Philips Hue Bridge Pro SQL Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge Pro. Although authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability, the existing authentication mechanism can be bypassed.

The specific flaw exists within the HTTP service, which listens on TCP port 443 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to construct SQL queries. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-33089.

MailEnable Save Directory Traversal Arbitrary File Creation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create arbitrary files on affected installations of MailEnable. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the implementation of the Save method. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-29161.

Movable Type provided by Six Apart Ltd. contains a code injection vulnerability in its Dynamic Publishing functionality. By sending a specially crafted request that is processed by the Dynamic Publishing, an attacker may be able to execute arbitrary PHP code on the affected product.

An unrestricted upload of files with dangerous type vulnerability in the Microchip TimePictra platform allows functionality not properly constrained by access control lists, potentially resulting in remote code execution.

Zohocorp ManageEngine AssetExplorer versions below 7860, ServiceDesk Plus versions below 15290, ServiceDesk Plus MSP versions below 15150, and SupportCenter Plus versions below 15150 are affected by a authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the Reports module. An authenticated user with the Create Query Reports permission could exploit specially crafted database queries to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying server.

Zohocorp ManageEngine M365 Manager Plus versions below 4818 is affected by an authenticated technician may exploit insufficient permission validation in the delegated administration interface to escalate privileges beyond their intended scope, which could result in remote code execution during administrative processing.

SeaweedFS before 4.42 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to probe local files by supplying a filesystem path in gcs_google_application_credentials. Attackers can send crafted gRPC FetchAndWriteNeedle requests and use differing error messages to learn file existence, readability, and partial content shape on the host.

A vulnerability in the GenericAdminAuthenticator component of Azul Payara Server and Azul Payara Micro allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to bypass JMX/RMI administrative access restrictions by spoofing the client host address. Successful exploitation can grant administrative access to the MBean server and lead to remote code execution. Azul Payara Micro is affected only when its JMX connector is enabled.

wallabag 2.3.3 before 2.6.16 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through article author metadata rendered with Twig raw in entry.html.twig. Attackers can embed HTML event handlers in a web page's author metadata so scripts run in a victim's wallabag session when the saved entry is opened, exposing their data.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.7 contain a reachable assertion vulnerability in ParsePFDEntry() that allows attackers to abort applications via an invalid orientation tag. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file with an out-of-range WMP_tagTransformation value to crash applications using default assertion-enabled builds, or store an unchecked orientation value otherwise.

Frappe CRM before 1.84.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the get_deal_contacts method that allows authenticated low-privileged users to read contacts of deals they cannot access. Attackers can supply or iterate CRM Deal names to obtain linked contacts' full names, email addresses, and mobile numbers, bypassing row-level permission rules.

Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 fails to validate the attachment_price field when creating posts, allowing authenticated users to set negative prices on charge attachments. Attackers with two ordinary accounts can download the attachment via GET /v1/attachment, where the negative price increases the buyer's wallet balance, minting funds to purchase other users' paid attachments.

REBUILD 2.7.0 through 4.5.4 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject AjQL conditions through the plan parameter of /project/tasks/list. Attackers can use priority-* plans and the returned task count as a boolean oracle to recover a task creator's SHA-256 password hash and log in as that user, including the administrator.

In Progress® Telerik® Reporting prior to version 20.3.26.1110, a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in the .NET Framework report designers allows a local attacker with low privileges to execute arbitrary code in the context of the designer process when the user performs certain editing operations.

OfficeCLI 1.0.56 through 1.0.161 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the officecli watch preview that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped numbering w:color values. Attackers can craft a DOCX whose color closes the style element, then abuse the unauthenticated /api/batch endpoint to read local files and modify the watched document.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows registered users to leak server-wide GitLab or Gitea tokens via repository_url. Attackers can create a gitlab or gitea project pointing to a controlled host and request its branches to capture the operator's token and reach internal hosts.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the fetchClientSecret Next.js server action that allows unauthenticated attackers to create Stripe checkout sessions for other teams. Attackers can invoke the action with a forged Team object containing a victim's stripeCustomerId to obtain Growth plan Checkout session client secrets with attacker-influenced return URLs.

Cetmix Tower through 17.0.3.0.0 and 18.0 before 18.0.4.0.1 contains an improper SSH host key verification vulnerability in SSHConnection.connect() that falls back to Paramiko's AutoAddPolicy when no host key is pinned. On-path attackers using ARP or DNS spoofing can present their own host key during Skip Host Key or Get from Host connections to capture stored SSH passwords and tamper with commands and files.

In Telerik UI for WinForms, versions prior to 2026.4.1111, an improper control of code generation vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to supply a crafted expression and execute unauthorized code in the context of the affected application.

In Telerik UI for WinForms, versions prior to 2026.4.1111, a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to perform unauthorized actions in the context of the affected application.

In Telerik UI for WPF, versions prior to 2026.4.1110, an improper control of code generation vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to execute unauthorized code in the context of the affected application.

In Telerik UI for WPF, versions prior to 2026.4.1110, a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to perform unauthorized actions in the context of the affected application.

In Progress® Telerik® UI for .NET MAUI prior to version 16.0.0, an untrusted URL redirection vulnerability in the RadRichTextEditor hyperlink handling and the RadPdfViewer link annotation handling allows an unauthenticated attacker to launch arbitrary operating system protocol handlers with attacker-controlled arguments via a crafted document or PDF link with a non-allowlisted URI scheme that the user opens.

In Telerik UI for WinForms, versions prior to 2026.4.1111, an untrusted URL redirection vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to launch arbitrary operating system protocol handlers with attacker-controlled arguments via crafted documents and hyperlinks with a non-allowlisted URI scheme that the user opens.

In Telerik UI for WPF, versions prior to 2026.4.1110, an untrusted URL redirection vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to launch arbitrary operating system protocol handlers with attacker-controlled arguments via crafted documents and hyperlinks with a non-allowlisted URI scheme that the user opens.

Dell SmartFabric OS10 Software, versions prior to 10.6.0.10, contains an Incorrect Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command execution.

Dell PowerStore contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. An authenticated user with limited privileges could potentially exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to privilege escalation to root on the appliance.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiOS 7.4 all versions, FortiOS 7.2 all versions, FortiOS 7.0 all versions may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or command via crafted packets.

Stored XSS via avatar upload chained with an authentication bypass in /Attachments leads to ATO
in Cervantes version v1.3-beta could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code in another user's browser with elevated privileges

The Cloud Storage Manager for Fluent Forms – Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, S3 Uploads plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.0. This is due to missing authorization checks on the `connection/{driver}/save` and `/download/single-file` REST endpoints, combined with insufficient path validation in the Google Drive `downloadFile()` function, where the Google Drive metadata `name` value is concatenated into a local path without `basename()`, `sanitize_file_name()`, or canonical path validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to store attacker-controlled Google Drive credentials, trigger a download of an attacker-owned file whose provider-returned filename contains path traversal, and write attacker-controlled content outside the intended `downloads` directory. When the written file has a PHP extension and lands in a web-accessible location, this can lead to remote code execution.
vp: cloud storage manager for fluent forms – google drive, dropbox, onedrive, s3 uploads

cves.d: The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'sort' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Successful exploitation requires the existence of at least one Peer-to-Peer campaign. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82663 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.5. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know or discover an existing campaign and team ID to modify the team's name, story, goal, access and notification settings, set its profile image URL, and upload WordPress-allowed media files as parentless attachments. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82568 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

A vulnerability has been identified in Rexroth IndraWorks. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the user’s system by parsing a manipulated file, because the file parser fails to properly sanitize the path name(s) or references embedded in the manipulated file. Exploitation requires user interaction, specifically opening a specially crafted file, which then causes the application to traverse outside the target directory and to write files in unauthorized locations, eventually enabling Remote Code Execution (RCE). This can lead to a complete compromise of the system running Rexroth IndraWorks.

An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2026x could lead to an unauthenticated remote code execution.

The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server dispatches some requests to REST endpoints configured for HTTP Basic authentication without verifying credentials. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke protected resources, bypassing authentication. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server with Basic authentication are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.

The JDBC based JAAS login module accepts a login without a password for accounts whose stored password is NULL. A remote attacker who knows the user name of such an account can authenticate as that user and obtain its roles. Only deployments using this login module with NULL passwords in the user table are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
Improper privilege management in TransitionPlayer prior to SMR Nov-2026 Release 1 allows local privileged attackers to execute arbitrary code with launcher privilege.

Cleartext transmission of sensitive information in the Agent of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before version 2024 SU8 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to in a MITM position to read and modify HTTP traffic.

Improper input validation in libMyFilterPlugin.camera.samsung.so prior to SMR Nov-2026 Release 1 allows local attackers to potentially execute arbitrary code. User interaction is required for triggering this vulnerability.
Stack-based buffer overflow in libsecuibc.so prior to SMR Nov-2026 Release 1 allows local attackers to execute arbitrary code.
Out-of-bounds write in libiosotglib.so prior to version 3.7.73.4 allows physical attackers to execute arbitrary code. User interaction is required for triggering this vulnerability.
Incorrect permission assignment for critical resource in Samsung Update prior to version 3.0.111.0 allows local attackers to execute arbitrary code.
Unquoted search path or element in Samsung Device Care prior to version 4.0.80 allows local attackers to execute arbitrary code.

When a non-default stateful session bean passivation strategy is configured, passivated bean state is written to predictably named files in the shared system temporary directory, reusing files that already exist there, and is deserialized on activation. A local attacker who can write to that directory can read passivated session state or supply data that the server deserializes, potentially leading to code execution as the server process. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the dr_mp3 drmp3_init_internal functionality of dr_libs (version(s): 0.7.3). A specially crafted .mp3 file can lead to an out-of-bounds read. An attacker can provide a malicious file to trigger this vulnerability.

A out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists in the dr_wav drwav__read_cue_to_metadata_obj functionality of dr_libs (version(s): 0.14.5). A specially crafted .wav file can lead to an out-of-bounds write. An attacker can provide a malicious file to trigger this vulnerability.

Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.30.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the validate() function of api/v1/index.php that allows attackers holding a password-recovery token and a predictable legacy signature to obtain valid remote-API authorization without a proper API key. Attackers can exploit this flaw via the POST /cronjobsusers/ endpoint to add arbitrary cron commands and achieve command execution as the affected hosting account, and can also abuse the same token to access global account-list and account-detail routes exposing usernames, contact emails, and password hashes.

Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('PHP Remote File Inclusion') vulnerability in Fuelthemes Werkstatt werkstatt allows PHP Local File Inclusion.This issue affects Werkstatt: from n/a before 4.8.16.

When MicroProfile JWT authentication is used for servlets that declare a run-as identity, the security state established for a request is not always cleared from the processing thread when the request does not complete normally. A remote attacker holding a valid token can cause later, unrelated requests served by the same thread to invoke enterprise beans with the elevated run-as identity. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

A negative MicroProfile JWT clock skew setting is not rejected and disables validation of the token expiration and other time-based claims. In such configurations, an attacker in possession of an expired token can still authenticate with it. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

When MicroProfile JWT role-based access control is used, the access constraints of JAX-RS resources are not always enforced as declared: resources that declare an empty set of allowed roles are accessible to every caller, resource classes that inherit the same method from a common superclass share their constraints, and class-level constraints declared on a superclass are ignored. A remote attacker can invoke resources that should be denied to them, in some configurations without authentication. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
Cleartext storage of sensitive information in Ivanti UWM before version 2026.4 allows a local authenticated attacker to retrieve another local user's session token.

After a successful WS-Security UsernameToken authentication, the caller identity stays associated with the worker thread once the request completes when web services are served by the standalone OpenEJB HTTP server. A remote unauthenticated attacker whose request is later processed on the same thread can invoke protected EJB methods with the identity of a previously authenticated user. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

The embedded server generates HTTP session identifiers with a non-cryptographic random number generator by default. A remote attacker who observes a session identifier can predict the identifiers issued to other users and hijack their sessions, if the application relies on HTTP sessions for authentication. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

The Jakarta Security OpenID Connect authentication mechanism generates the state and nonce values with a non-cryptographic random number generator and insufficient entropy. A remote attacker who predicts these values can forge an authentication callback that logs a victim into the attacker's account, and the replay protection for ID tokens is weakened. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store accepts an empty password as valid if the directory server allows unauthenticated binds, which some directory servers do by default. A remote attacker can then authenticate as any existing user without knowing the password. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store does not neutralize special characters in the caller name before using it in directory queries. A remote unauthenticated attacker can alter the queries to enumerate accounts, infer directory attribute values, or influence which directory entry the login is validated against. Only applications using the LDAP identity store are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

Authentication configured for an EJB JAX-WS endpoint in the TomEE deployment descriptor is not enforced when the endpoint is published within an existing web application. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the web service operations, unless the application protects the endpoint with its own web.xml security constraints or EJB method permissions. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

@fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart and url-encoded form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, the url-encoded parser stops accumulating a field only when the decoded length exactly equals the configured per-field size limit, and a malformed percent escape is passed through verbatim by the decoder, so the decoded length can jump from just below the limit to just above it and skip that equality check. The parser then keeps buffering the field in memory until the next delimiter or the end of the request, so a single unauthenticated url-encoded field or field name can grow to the size of the whole request body regardless of a much smaller configured per-field limit, with memory use bounded only by the independent whole-request body limit. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which clamps a field as soon as the decoded length reaches or exceeds the limit, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, set a conservative whole-request body limit so the per-field overshoot cannot exceed it.

The security constraint generated for EJB JAX-WS endpoints with configured authentication protects only some HTTP methods. A remote unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication by sending requests with another HTTP method. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

@fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, a multipart part whose header block is never terminated before the next boundary is counted by the vendored Dicer parser as an open part that never ends, so the parser emits neither a finish nor an error event and the request hangs. A single unauthenticated request of roughly one hundred bytes triggers the stall, and through @fastify/multipart the hung handler is not released when the client disconnects, so repeated requests leak handlers and whatever resources they hold, such as files, database connections and concurrency slots, until the process is restarted. The same parser is reached by the formData methods of undici versions 5.25.3 through 6.7.0. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, configure Fastify's handler timeout so hung handlers are eventually terminated and their resources released.

The internal system EJBs used for remote deployment and configuration did not enforce their administrative role check when the server ran with the default profile. A remote unauthenticated attacker able to reach the remote EJB endpoint could deploy arbitrary applications and execute code. Only installations that enabled the system applications and a remote EJB endpoint are exposed. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

Stateful session bean identifiers are not generated from a cryptographically secure random source. A remote attacker with access to the EJB remote endpoint who holds one valid identifier can derive those of other clients' sessions and invoke methods on their beans, exposing or modifying other users' session state. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

@fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 7.4.0 through 10.1.8, when the plugin is registered with the attachFieldsToBody option, the saveRequestFiles helper treats any object in the parsed request body that carries truthy file and buffer properties as an uploaded file. An unauthenticated client can forge such an object through a plain JSON request or a JSON-typed multipart field, so attacker-chosen bytes are written to the temporary directory while upload hooks and the file count and size limits are skipped, and the saved entry keeps the attacker's filename verbatim instead of being reduced to its basename. Because that filename can contain parent directory segments, applications that use it as a write destination, as the project README example does, are exposed to an arbitrary relative-path file write from a single request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.9, and users should upgrade to 10.1.9 or later. As a workaround, call saveRequestFiles only after confirming the request is multipart, and reduce each returned filename to its basename or validate it against an allowlist before using it as a destination.

The stateful session bean passivation mechanism derives the on-disk file name from a client-supplied identifier without validating it. A remote attacker with access to the remote EJB service can cause session state to be read from or written to files outside the passivation directory. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.

@fastify/proxy-addr determines which network hops are trusted proxies and backs Fastify's trustProxy setting, so that forwarded headers can be believed. In versions 3.0.0 through 5.1.2, when trustProxy is configured with a zoned IPv6 link-local address, the trust comparison checks only the address bits and ignores the zone identifier, so a host on another link of a multi-homed server that carries the same link-local address is trusted as well. Such an attacker can spoof the X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers, making the client IP, host and protocol reported by Fastify attacker-chosen values and defeating IP allowlists, rate limiting and audit logging. Exploitation requires a multi-homed server whose trustProxy is a zoned link-local address and an attacker directly on one of its other links; the default configuration and global, private or loopback trust entries are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/proxy-addr 5.1.3, and users should upgrade to 5.1.3 or later. As a workaround, avoid trusting a zoned link-local address on a multi-homed host and trust a global, private or loopback proxy address instead.

The sourcecache expansion module in MISP Modules (misp-modules) contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. When a user with permission to create or modify attributes of type 'link' or 'url' submits an attribute value, the module passes the URL directly to its internal archiving function without any validation of the target address. An attacker can therefore craft a URL pointing to loopback addresses (e.g., 127.0.0.1), private network ranges, link-local addresses, or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., 169.254.169.254). The MISP server will issue an HTTP request to that target and store the response body in the event, effectively exfiltrating data from internal services to the attacker through the MISP interface. Non-HTTP schemes such as file:// are also accepted, potentially allowing local file disclosure. The vulnerability requires an authenticated MISP user with the ability to create or edit attributes of the affected types. The security impact is information disclosure from internal services reachable by the MISP server, including sensitive data such as cloud credentials, internal application data, or local files.

The Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 was distributed with a hidden update mechanism that fetched Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 updates from its author's own server instead of WordPress.org, which was used to push a backdoored build to sites, allowing the attacker controlling that server to inject arbitrary content into pages and to deliver arbitrary code to affected sites.

Version 5.2.1, as published on WordPress.org, bundled the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker library (updater/ directory) configured to poll https://anadnet.com/updates/?action=get_metadata&slug=quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4. In March 2021 that server delivered a modified 5.2.3 build, different from the 5.2.3 later published on WordPress.org, which kept the update channel and added a the_content filter that, for logged-out visitors on single posts and pages, fetched content from https://w.anadnet.com/bro/3/ (passing the site host, request URI and visitor User-Agent) and prepended the response to the post (observed serving SEO spam links to search engine crawlers). Because the version string matched a later WordPress.org release, affected sites were not offered a clean update until 5.2.4.

Indicators of compromise:
- Outbound requests to anadnet.com or w.anadnet.com
- An updater/ directory (Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker, Puc v4p10) inside wp-content/Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/
- The strings filter_the_content_in_the_main_loop, ppr_pro, QQQEND or w.anadnet.com in page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php
- page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php with MD5 ad717da18cf8a2b69899c0d7dafee05a (tampered 5.2.3)

Remediation: remove the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 (it has been closed on WordPress.org), or at minimum reinstall the clean 5.2.4 from WordPress.org, delete any leftover updater/ directory, verify the files with "wp Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 verify-checksums quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4", clear the opcode cache, and treat any site that ran the tampered build as potentially compromised.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: Zero out sring pointers on unmap

If xenvif_map_frontend_data_rings() fails when a ring is already mapped,
it unmaps them via xenvif_unmap_frontend_data_rings() which keeps the
ring pointers unchanged. xenvif_connect_data()'s cleanup path calls
xenvif_disconnect_queue() which in turn calls
xenvif_unmap_frontend_data_rings() again, which will attempt to unmap the
pointers a second time.

Zero out the ring pointers after they are unmapped to avoid this issue.

This is XSA-532

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: Fix XenBus connection failure cleanup

xenvif_get_stats and xenvif_get_ethtool_stats capture vif->num_queues
under rcu_read_lock. We need to unpublish vif->num_queues before
synchronize_net to ensure that readers that come afterwards will not
read a non-zero vif->num_queues and attempt to access invalid queues.

This is the same cleanup algorithm as used in backend_disconnect and
added in commit b17075d5c198 ("xen-netback: fix race condition on XenBus
disconnect").

This is XSA-531

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()

When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains
other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash
like:

 Oops: general protection fault
 KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access
 RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503)
 Call Trace:
  vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419)
  do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583)
  __x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602)

This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return
value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through
udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being
treated as a folio pointer with obvious results.

Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either
0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids
without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under
cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched
creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner.

  nfsd4_exchange_id
  nfsd4_proc_compound
  nfsd_dispatch
  svc_process

list.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()

When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct
smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed,
Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This
only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So
the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd.

    unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset);
    int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset;

    if (!dacl_offset ||
	(dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size))
	    goto out;

Commit beff0bc9d69b ("ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check")
fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out,
because it is only valid for 32-bit builds.

SET_INFO(SEC) with dacloffset=0xfffffff8, then QUERY_INFO(SEC) on the
same file:

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow

High-speed devices with out of spec 1024 byte bulk endpoints exist and
are allowed by USB core, but xhci-hcd always sets packet size to 512.
The exact nature of these devices isn't documented, commit fb5ee84ea72c
("USB: Accept bulk endpoints with 1024-byte maxpacket") only states
that they "don't work with xHCI host controllers", whatever it means.

But somebody (or a malicious device) can try, and then the driver will
allocate a 512 byte bounce buffer for this endpoint and may write up to
1024 bytes into it if particular scatter-gather URBs are used, because
xhci_align_td() obtains packet size from the descriptor. Fix this.

As a side effect, TRBs will be aligned to the packet size chosen by the
driver on all endpoints of all speeds. Alignment serves the xHC, not
device, so this is fine. Only out of spec devices are affected anyway.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease

parse_reply_info_lease() reads a 32-bit struct_len off the wire and only
checks that many bytes are present, without requiring struct_len to cover
sizeof(struct ceph_mds_reply_lease) (10 bytes).  A malicious MDS can
declare a shorter record and still get the pointer published: the
following *p += sizeof(**lease) overshoot is undone by *p = lend, so
nothing downstream rejects the reply.  ceph_fill_trace() ->
update_dentry_lease() then reads 10 bytes through that pointer on any
lookup on a mounted CephFS, running past the end of the message front.

Require the record to cover the structure, matching the sibling
parse_reply_info_dir().  A conforming MDS always encodes the full 10
bytes.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks

check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks
it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire:
ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then
overwrites it with the size of the "in" set.  Neither is bounded by
CEPH_MAX_MDS, only by m_info allocating, so a monitor announcing more ranks
than the bitmap holds makes test_bit() read past the end of targets[].  The
clear_bit() loop above indexes the same bitmap, though it is additionally
bounded by mdsc->max_sessions.  The map arrives on the monitor connection,
which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode.

CEPH_MAX_MDS is a protocol constant from src/mds/mdstypes.h, and the
reserved inode ranges in super.h are laid out one rank apart over that
span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt.  Reject it where the rank
space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fbdev: udlfb: don't rebuild the mode list while the framebuffer is in use

dlfb_setup_modes() frees info->modelist with fb_destroy_modelist() and
rebuilds it, but fbcon holds raw pointers into that list in
fb_display[i].mode and nothing un-publishes them the way
do_unregister_framebuffer() and store_modes() do with
fbcon_delete_modelist(). The function does refuse to install a new mode
while the framebuffer has users (dlfb->fb_count != 0), but only after the
list is already destroyed. Reached from the 0666 "edid" sysfs attribute,
an unprivileged write to /sys/class/graphics/fb0/edid therefore fails with

fbcon_open(), so that condition covers exactly the states in which

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check

ceph_update_snap_trace() bounds the two encoded snapid arrays that follow a
struct ceph_mds_snap_realm with sizeof(u64) * (num_snaps +
num_prior_parent_snaps).  Both counts come straight off the wire as __le32,
so the addition is evaluated in unsigned int and wraps before sizeof(u64)
promotes it to size_t: an MDS sending num_snaps = 1 and
num_prior_parent_snaps = 0xffffffff makes the sum zero and the check
degenerates to ceph_decode_need(&p, e, 0, bad), which always passes.
dup_array() then reads num_snaps * 8 bytes past the end of the message
front, which ceph_msg_new2() allocates at exactly front_len bytes.  An
unsolicited CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_SNAP reaches this from a malicious or
compromised MDS with no client-side action, as do the snaptraces carried in
an MDS reply and in a cap import.

Compute the length with size_add()/size_mul() so it saturates at SIZE_MAX
instead of wrapping, in the style fs/ceph/mdsmap.c already uses for
num_export_targets.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

virtio_net: atomically disable rx mode work

virtio-net uses a boolean to gate rx_mode_work during device teardown.
The flag is changed under RTNL, but ndo_set_rx_mode checks it under the
address-list lock. A callback can therefore pass the check and enqueue work
after teardown has flushed it. The work is also enabled before late
probe operations that can fail, allowing probe unwind to free the netdev
with work still queued.

KASAN reports the worker using a virtqueue that probe unwind already freed:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in virtqueue_add_split
  Workqueue: events virtnet_rx_mode_work
  Call Trace:
   virtqueue_add_split (drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c:706)
   virtqueue_add_sgs (drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c:2839)
   virtnet_send_command_reply (drivers/net/virtio_net.c:3565)
   virtnet_rx_mode_work (drivers/net/virtio_net.c:3833)
   process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3322)
   worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3405)
  Freed by task 119:
   kfree (mm/slub.c:6625)
   vp_del_vq.isra.0 (drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_common.c:259)
   vp_del_vqs (drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_common.c:285)
   virtnet_probe (drivers/net/virtio_net.c:7129)

Use the workqueue disable mechanism to atomically reject new queue attempts
and drain running work. Keep work disabled until probe succeeds or restore
has reattached the netdev, then enable it and replay receive-mode state for
a running interface. Disable it before resource teardown in freeze and
remove.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: go7007: only set audio_enabled if go7007_snd_init() succeeded

go7007_register_encoder() sets go->audio_enabled before calling
go7007_snd_init() and discards its return value.  go7007_snd_init()
assigns go->snd_context only on success, so a failed ALSA setup leaves
audio_enabled set with snd_context still NULL.  The disconnect path tests
audio_enabled and calls go7007_snd_remove(), which dereferences
snd_context unconditionally.

go7007_snd_init() returns -ENODEV once its never-decremented static card
counter reaches SNDRV_CARDS, so SNDRV_CARDS attach/detach cycles arm the
next attach; no memory pressure is needed.

Set go->audio_enabled only once go7007_snd_init() has succeeded.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len

handle_command_ack() bounds the decode with msg->front_alloc_len, the size
of the reply buffer, instead of msg->front.iov_len, the number of bytes the
monitor sent.  mon_alloc_msg() routes every CEPH_MSG_MON_COMMAND_ACK to
get_generic_reply(), which returns the preallocated ->reply of whichever
generic request carries the same tid, so the buffer keeps its fixed size
however short the reply is.  An ack with hdr.front_len below sizeof(struct
ceph_mon_request_header) + sizeof(u32), including 0, still passes
ceph_decode_need(), and ceph_decode_32() returns four bytes that were never
received: uninitialized slab memory, stale bytes of an earlier message, or
bytes the peer planted by sending a reply that lands in the same buffer and
is then rejected.  The read stays within the allocation, so KASAN does not
flag it.

req->result reaches userspace through ceph_monc_do_statfs(),
ceph_monc_get_version() and ceph_monc_blocklist_add(); rbd hands it back
from write() on /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major, and rbd_get_client() passes
it to ERR_PTR() unchecked, which faults:

  rbd: failed to get latest osdmap: -186318427
  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfffe9ca034
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  RIP: 0010:do_rbd_add (drivers/block/rbd.c:7105)
  Call Trace:
   ...
   kernfs_fop_write_iter (fs/kernfs/file.c:345)
   vfs_write (fs/read_write.c:595 fs/read_write.c:687)
   ksys_write (fs/read_write.c:739)
   do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:61 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:84)
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121)
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Use msg->front.iov_len, matching handle_subscribe_ack(),
handle_statfs_reply(), handle_get_version_reply() and handle_auth_reply().
A well-formed ack has front.iov_len >= 22 and is unaffected; a short one
takes the existing bad: path.  This applies commit d3c32939fa0e ("libceph:
bound get_version reply decode to front len") to the last decode-side
use of front_alloc_len in this file.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nft_fwd_netdev: use recursion counter in neigh egress path

nft_fwd_neigh can be used in egress chains (NF_NETDEV_EGRESS). When the
forwarding rule targets the same device or two devices forward to each
other, neigh_xmit() triggers dev_queue_xmit() which re-enters
nf_hook_egress(), causing infinite recursion and stack overflow.

Move the nf_get_nf_dup_skb_recursion() accessor and NF_RECURSION_LIMIT
to the shared header nf_dup_netdev.h as a static inline, so that
nft_fwd_netdev can use the recursion counter directly without exported
function call overhead. Guard neigh_xmit() with the same recursion
limit already used in nf_do_netdev_egress().

[ Updated to cache the nf_get_nf_dup_skb_recursion pointer. --pablo ]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()

In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after
commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group
rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or
5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace)
on posix).

However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() ->
copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total),
and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes)
even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security
descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or
dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past
the end of the slab buffer.

Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of
id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix SMB2 CREATE response buffer overflow

smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() uses the MAX_CIFS_SMALL_BUFFER_SIZE
(448-byte) buffer for a single SMB2_CREATE response. That buffer also
holds a 4-byte length field, which only leaves 444 bytes for the SMB2
body.

The AAPL response made this buffer too small. After 8f1b796ff113, a
request with AAPL response contexts may need at least 456 bytes. In
the 456-byte case, create_aapl_rsp_buf() is appended last, clears 128
bytes, and writes 12 bytes past the allocation.

KASAN reports:

    BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    Write of size 128 at addr ffff88800370954c by task kworker/0:0/9
    ...
    create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    smb2_open+0x58f9/0xef10
    ...
    smb2_allocate_rsp_buf+0x19d/0x370
    ...
    The buggy address is located 332 bytes inside of
     allocated 448-byte region [ffff888003709400, ffff8880037095c0)

Reserve enough space for any fixed CREATE response KSMBD can build.
Store the required allocation size in the per-dialect values table.
This keeps the small buffer for other commands and avoids using the max
transaction buffer for every CREATE.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect

ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the
reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry.
If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to
remove the volatile id.

Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before
either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops
its references first, the other request makes the final put through
ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first
session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed
memory.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
  Call Trace:
   __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 1030:
   __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd]

Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file
lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not
one made by another holder.

Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path,
before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the
request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which
holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup
is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix app-instance non-durable supersede session UAF

ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id() supersedes a prior open that has the
same AppInstanceId. It reaches that open's session through opinfo->sess.
This pointer is not refcounted.

Session teardown detaches durable handles before it frees the session.
It does not detach a non-durable open. That open still points at the
session through opinfo->sess after the session is freed. Another session
can supersede the open at the same time. The supersede then takes a
write lock through the stale pointer, in the freed session's file table.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
  Call Trace:
   _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
   ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id+0xd9/0x670 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x3e10/0xd910 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 212:
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0x38d/0x480 [ksmbd]

Fix this by looking the session up by opinfo->session_id. The lookup
returns a reference, as smb2_break_collect_channels() does. Recheck that
opinfo->sess still points at it before using it.

Do the lookup without m_lock held. destroy_previous_session() takes
m_lock under the session table lock, and taking them in the other order
here would deadlock.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups

TCP established ehash lookups are lockless. The socket caches involved
use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU, so memory can be reused before an RCU reader
that retained its old address has finished.

After a tuple match, __inet_lookup_established() and
__inet6_lookup_established() acquire a reference and repeat the tuple
check. They do not check whether the new object is hashed. If the
address is reused for a socket with the same tuple, the lookup can
acquire a reference to the new object and return it while its nulls node
is unhashed.

A PoC that drives reuse with a SYN cookie request socket reproduced the
crash. The new request socket is unhashed and has a NULL rsk_listener.
A lookup that had loaded the address of the old request socket acquired
the reference published by tcp_get_cookie_sock() and returned the new
object. tcp_v4_rcv() then read sk_state through the NULL listener.

The resulting crash was:

  #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
  #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page

  ...
  RIP: 0010:tcp_v4_rcv+0x44e/0x1280
  ...
  R10: 0000000000000001 R11: 00000000024ca8c0 R12: 0000000000000000
  ...
  CR2: 0000000000000012 CR3: 0000000103d50004 CR4: 0000000000770ef0
  ...
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   ? raw_local_deliver+0xae/0x240
   ip_protocol_deliver_rcu+0x2d/0x180
   ip_local_deliver_finish+0x84/0x100
   ip_sublist_rcv_finish+0x5f/0x70
   ip_sublist_rcv+0x12a/0x1d0
   ip_list_rcv+0xfd/0x130
   __netif_receive_skb_list_core+0x223/0x250
   netif_receive_skb_list_internal+0x1d2/0x2c0
   ? try_fill_recv+0x39/0x7b0
   napi_complete_done+0x74/0x170
   virtnet_poll+0x445/0x600
   __napi_poll+0x27/0x1e0
   net_rx_action+0x2fe/0x3b0
   handle_softirqs+0xc2/0x2c0
   __irq_exit_rcu+0x74/0xd0
   common_interrupt+0x7f/0x90
